yoga_sutras.translation: Perfection in samadhi results from devotion to Ishvara — the Supreme Being.

commentary.text: By surrender to God — not the mere repetition of His name, but true surrender — the mind becomes steady and meditation deepens naturally into samadhi.
Ishvara Pranidhana is the crown of niyama. When the ego submits to the divine will, the practitioner transcends personal limitation and touches the infinite.
Surrender is not weakness — it is the ultimate intelligence. When you stop insisting that existence goes your way, it starts working for you in ways you could not have planned.

yoga_sutras.translation: Yoga is the cessation of the fluctuations of the mind.

commentary.text: The mind, like a lake, reflects the Self when its surface is calm. Yoga is the stilling of the waves — not their suppression, but their natural settling.
The moment you stop the inner noise — the constant commentary, judgment, desire — what remains is not emptiness but presence. That presence is yoga.
You don't need to stop thoughts. Simply stop identifying with them. The identification is the chitta vritti. Recognise the one who watches — that is already stillness.

bhagavad_gita.translation: That state where the mind finds its rest through the practice of yoga — where one sees the Self through the Self — and remains in infinite bliss.

commentary.text: This is the experiential peak of the Gita's yoga: not a doctrine but a state — the mind resting in itself, freed from its restless outward seeking, knowing its own deepest nature as ananda.
Krishna is not describing a religious experience — he is describing a psychological transformation. When the mind finds its natural stillness, even ordinary life becomes extraordinary.
This resting of the mind is not separation from life — it is full presence within it. The yogi does not withdraw from the world but meets it with unshakeable peace.

upanishads.translation: Not inward-knowing, not outward-knowing, not both — the fourth (Turiya) is pure consciousness itself.

commentary.text: Turiya is not a state you enter — it is what you always are. The three states (waking, dream, sleep) are superimpositions upon this fourth, which is ever-present consciousness.
You have always been the Turiya. You do not need to achieve it — you need only stop pretending to be limited. That pretending is the ego, and its end is liberation.
The Mandukya points not to a withdrawal from life but to its fullest living — action arising from the ground of pure awareness, undisturbed by the ripples of circumstance.

hatha_yoga_pradipika.translation: We consider meditation on Nada (inner sound) to be the single most important practice of Raja Yoga.

commentary.text: The Hatha Yoga Pradipika dedicates its fourth chapter entirely to Nada — the vibration that underlies all creation. To hear the inner sound is to hear the universe speaking through you.
Sound is the subtlest of all sense objects. When external hearing is withdrawn and the yogi listens to the inner Nada, the fluctuations of the mind are absorbed into the vibration itself.
Every sound in the universe has a corresponding inner frequency. Nada yoga is not about hearing music — it is about recognising that you yourself are a living instrument of the cosmos.
